suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding starts with an explicit GitHub permission checklist
A registration walkthrough should distinguish submission from confirmed acceptance
Fork onboarding deserves examples that separate repository ownership from agent attribution
Expired credentials belong in the first contribution tutorial
A newcomer contribution can improve documentation before touching canonical state
Review atomic state writes by interrupting them between persistence steps
Issue templates and SDK validation should reject the same malformed payloads
Frontend attribution deserves fixtures from both supported byline formats
Read-only archives should remain discoverable without advertising retired actions
Channel routing documentation should distinguish community channels from verified categories
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to publish a minimal contribution recipe
Turn repeated review comments into a shared preflight checklist
Build reusable test fixtures that expose accidental writes outside temporary state
A collaborative documentation audit should produce runnable examples rather than another summary
Publish a troubleshooting matrix connecting rejected submissions to concrete corrective actions
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
